thread.title: Here are all the new ways Apple will help you combat your smartphone addiction in iOS 12 (AAPL)

author: Avery Hartmans
title: Here are all the new ways Apple will help you combat your smartphone addiction in iOS 12 (AAPL)
text:
WWDC 2018 ios 12 bedtime More Apple
Apple introduced new tools to combat smartphone addiction at WWDC, its annual developer conference. The new tools allow you to set limits on how much you're using certain apps, group your notifications, and enable "Do Not Disturb during bedtime." Parents will also be able to set and manage limits on their kids' iPhone and iPad use as well. Apple wants to help cure your smartphone addiction.
At Apple's annual developer conference on Monday, vice president of software engineering Craig Federighi unveiled new tools to help you cut back on your screen time, along with new controls for parents.
Here's everything Apple announced:
Do Not Disturb during bedtime . Turn on the feature before heading to bed and you won't see notifications until the next morning. When you pick up your phone during the night, it will only show the time. In the morning, you'll be "gently eased into your day" — when you're ready to see all your notifications, tap the screen. Set an end time for Do Not Disturb. By force touching on the Do Not Disturb button in your control center, you'll now see the option to set a specific end time. Turn off notifications for apps you’re no longer using. Your phone will alert you to apps you haven't used in a while and allow you to shut off notifications entirely. Grouped notifications. This is a big one! Now, your notifications will be grouped by the app they're sent from. Now, you can "triage" a whole group of notifications by swiping them away. Screen time. This feature will provide an activity summary that details how you used your iPhone or iPad over the course of a week. It will provide insight into how much time you're spending on your phone and where you're spending it, including which apps you're using, how many times you pick up your phone, what's drawing you in, and what's sending you the most notifications. App limits. You'll be able to set time limits for individual apps. When you spend a lot of time on an app like Instagram, your phone will send you an alert saying "5 minutes left on Instagram today." Once you’ve reached your limit, you’ll see a notification telling you to move on. New parental controls. Parents will now be able to get notifications about their kids' smartphone use. They'll be able to set limits for how long their kids are using certain apps, and cut off access to apps that aren't age appropriate. These updates will arrive on iPhones and iPads when iOS 12 arrives this fall.
